content.text:
Understood — no scheduled check-in; the PR subscription alone will wake me on any CI failure or comment.

**1 and 2 are implemented, tested red-first, and up as [PR #845](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/845)** (issue [#843](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/843), branch restarted from `main` since #839 merged). Full suite 1679/1679, both sweeps clean, CI running on the head and past its checkout — the unit-test step is the suite that just passed locally.

- **Fence-blind markdown scanning** — `scanIgnoringMarkdownFences: true` in [pattern-rules.mjs](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/claude/declarative-checks-review-tdg3by/engine/checks/helpers/pattern-rules.mjs): content assertions read markdown files with fenced blocks blanked (line count preserved — the same view `checkSections` always had, now shared as `blankMarkdownFences`); non-markdown files untouched. First customer: [`cer/readme-sections`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/claude/declarative-checks-review-tdg3by/packs/chrome-extension-release/declared-checks.json) — a `## Install` heading inside a fenced example no longer satisfies its `require`.
- **Count/occurrence primitive** — `countMatchingLines: [{ linesMatching, atLeast, atMost, what, fix }]`: per-file bounds on matching lines, Vale's `occurrence` idiom. `atMost: 0` forbids; too many anchors at the first line past the bound, too few at the file; bounds validated at load so a boundless entry can't silently assert nothing. First conversion customer is `scheduler-workflow-shape`'s cron legs, tracked in [#838](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/838).

**Candidate scan for 4 (@key addressing).** The only real customers are the three hand-rolled config validators — `growth-config`, `preferences-store-configured`, and barrier's config half — which all do exactly the @key move (unknown-property detection over an object's key names, plus per-key type asserts). But they read `ctx.config`, the loader's overlay, not a parsed tracked file, so a bare @key over files wouldn't reach them. Among file-shaped rules there are zero standalone customers: `node/earn-each-dependency` iterates dependency keys but is a base-vs-head work rule, and `adoption-answers-pending`/`seeds-agree` are cross-file joins. So my recommendation stands as before but sharper: don't add @key as a spec key; it arrives as the addressing vocabulary inside the pack-manifest config-schema seam (the review's ESLint `meta.schema` consolidation) when that lands — that one change carries all three validators.

**Candidate scan for 5 (declarative autofix).** Exactly one clean auto-apply candidate in the whole corpus: `generated-merge-driver`, whose fix is a fully determined append (`<base> merge=ours` into `.gitattributes`). Three more are suggestion-tier only, because the splice needs human content: `catalog-completeness` (the description column), `checkKeyValueFile`'s missing-key case (the value), `markdown-link-labels` (the label text). Everything else's remedy is judgment — move prose, cut words, restructure. One auto-applied customer fails the who-else-would-use-it test, so I recommend not building the fix machinery now; if a second determined-splice customer appears, markdownlint's `{lineNumber, editColumn, deleteCount, insertText}` data shape is the one that keeps specs pure JSON.

**How 3 (fixtures-as-data) looks in the end.** Beside each `declared-checks.json` sits a `declared-checks.fixtures.json`: per rule id, a list of cases — `{ "rule": "…", "files": { "path": "content", … }, "expectFindings": [{ "file", "line", "what" }] }` — where a valid case expects `[]`. One shared harness (an engine-test helper plus a single canon test that structurally discovers every fixtures file, the way `loadDeclaredChecks` discovers declarations) materializes each case's files into a temp repo, runs the real rule through the real engine, and asserts the findings including their message text — ESLint RuleTester's contract. The meta-check grows one finding: a declared check no fixture exercises. End state: authoring a check means writing two JSON files and no `.mjs`; see-it-fail becomes structural, because an invalid fixture that produces no finding fails the harness by construction; and member local packs inherit the same proof for free. Nothing of this is built — it's the design, awaiting your call.

> ⚠️ Still open: CI on #845 in progress (subscribed — failures wake me; local run of the same suite is green); the send_later check-in was declined so no timed re-check is armed; @key and autofix stand as analyzed, not built; #838 carries the deferred conversion slices.

input.body:
Implements the first two owner-approved redesign recommendations from the declarative-checks review (#838/#839), and the conversion they unlock. Closes #843.

- **`scanIgnoringMarkdownFences: true`** — content assertions (`matchLines`, `checkEachFile`, `repoWide`, `countMatchingLines`) read each markdown file with fenced code blocks blanked, line count preserved: the same view `checkSections` always had via `markdownIndex` (the fence pass is now the shared `blankMarkdownFences`). Non-markdown files are untouched. Adopter: `cer/readme-sections` — a `## Install` heading shown inside a fenced example no longer satisfies its `require`.
- **`countMatchingLines: [{ linesMatching, atLeast, atMost, what, fix }]`** — per scanned file, the number of matching lines must sit within the declared bounds (Vale's `occurrence` idiom). `atMost: 0` forbids the pattern; too many anchors at the first line past the bound, too few at the file; `{count}`/`{atLeast}`/`{atMost}` interpolate. Bounds validated at load, so a boundless entry cannot silently assert nothing. Counting respects the rule's `scanIgnoring*` view.
- **Conversion: `scheduler-workflow-shape`** is now fully declared — `countMatchingLines` carries the exactly-one-cron leg (its first customer), one `matchLines` entry the hourly `:10–:50` cron shape (the two imperative legs merged into one finding), and five `checkEachFile` requires the dispatch/concurrency/engine-entry/permission guards. The imperative module is deleted; its tests run through `loadDeclaredChecks`, with the cron-count cases added.

Not converted, and why: `markdown-link-labels` resolves link targets with real path math; `rules-line-length` and `task-phase-discipline` wait on `maxLineLength`/`andLineMatches` (#838's deferred keys) — fence-blindness was their precondition, not their whole unlock.

The two `scanIgnoring*` keys compose through one memoized per-visit view map. All engine tests written red-first; full suite 1681/1681, both sweeps clean (the declared-check-messages meta-check caught and forced a trim of this PR's own cron fix string).

input.body:
Implements the first two owner-approved redesign recommendations from the declarative-checks review (#838/#839), plus the conversions the new vocabulary unlocks — including #838's deferred key slice, pulled forward on owner request. Closes #843.

**New vocabulary** (all red-first tested in `engine-tests/pattern-rules.test.mjs`):

- **`scanIgnoringMarkdownFences: true`** — content assertions read each markdown file with fenced code blocks blanked, line count preserved (the view `checkSections` always had; the fence pass is now the shared `blankMarkdownFences`). Non-markdown files untouched; composes with `scanIgnoringComments` through one memoized per-visit view map.
- **`countMatchingLines: [{ linesMatching, atLeast, atMost, what, fix }]`** — per-file bounds on the number of matching lines (Vale's `occurrence` idiom); `atMost: 0` forbids; bounds validated at load.
- **`unlessPreviousLineMatches`** — a matchLines hit is excused when the line above matches (the first line has none).
- **`andLineMatches`** — a second pattern that must also hit the same line.
- **`whenPathMatches`** — per-assertion path scoping, so one rule covers two file families without cross-firing.
- **`maxLineLength: { bytes, what, fix }`** — one finding per file at the first over-long line, byte-measured.

**Conversions** (four imperative modules deleted; every test now drives the declared rule through the real engine):

- `scheduler-workflow-shape` — `countMatchingLines`' first customer (exactly-one-cron), one `matchLines` for the hourly `:10–:50` shape, five `checkEachFile` requires.
- `warning-suppression` — seven bare-marker patterns, each excused by an explaining line above via `unlessPreviousLineMatches`; the shared remedy is the rule-level `fix`.
- `rules-line-length` — `maxLineLength` at 100 bytes over `RULES.md` files.
- `task-phase-discipline` — the skip∧condition conjunction via `andLineMatches`, its two file families (`task.md` instructions, prework workers) split by `whenPathMatches`.
- `cer/readme-sections` adopts `scanIgnoringMarkdownFences` — a heading inside a fenced example no longer satisfies its `require`.

Conversions verified finding-for-finding against the live tree: the world sweep's profile is unchanged (0 blocking, 28 advisory, same anchors). Not converted, and why: `markdown-link-labels` resolves link targets with real path math; the remaining ~50 imperative rules have the structural causes recorded in `docs/declarative-checks/REVIEW.md` §4.

Full suite 1686/1686, both sweeps clean (the declared-check-messages meta-check caught and forced a trim of this PR's own cron fix string).

name: merge-to-main
description: Merge the change in front of the owner into main. Use when the owner says "LGTM" or asks to merge/land the current branch or PR into main.
---


The portable recipe for landing the change in front of the owner on `main` — the *mechanics* behind the owner's merge-to-main command (the owner's preferences own the trigger *phrase*; this file owns the *how*). Invoked through the `merge-to-main` skill (this skill); this doc stays the canonical recipe.

**A project's bespoke merge policy overrides this default.** Most projects need nothing here — this default is the whole story. A project that genuinely diverges (a different merge method, a CI/twice-green gate, an extra approval) **states so by naming its merge-policy file explicitly in its own `CLAUDE.md`**. When that declaration is present, read that file first and let it override the divergent points below; when it's absent, follow this default as-is. Don't go hunting for a policy file that the project's `CLAUDE.md` doesn't name.

## Recipe (~4 calls)

1. Load both GitHub tools in **one** `ToolSearch`: `create_pull_request` + `merge_pull_request`.
2. No PR open for the branch yet? `create_pull_request` (base `main`); end the body with `Closes #<issue>`, and take the PR number from the returned URL.
3. Gate on CI **only if the repo has it** — a workflow that actually runs on PRs/pushes. `workflow_call`-only reusable workflows (this repo hosts some) are *not* CI: they never run here, so a non-empty `.github/workflows/` alone proves nothing; check the PR for check runs instead. No CI → no gate; don't wait for checks that will never come.
4. `merge_pull_request`, `merge_method: squash`, title `<subject> (#<pr>)`. Merge directly — don't pre-read status; the call fails loudly if it isn't mergeable.
5. Sync local `main`: `git checkout main && git pull origin main`.

The two divergent points — **`squash`** as the method and **CI gating** — are exactly what a bespoke policy file changes.

## After the merge: capture the conversation (every session, every user)

Once the merge has landed and local `main` is synced, run the growth pack's capture step:
`node .claudinite/shared/packs/grow_with_claudinite/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>` (from the canon repo itself: `node packs/grow_with_claudinite/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`), `<n>` being the issue your `Closes #<issue>` named. Deterministic, seconds-long; it pushes the conversation to the orphan `conversation-logs` branch. It runs **here, in-session, because it needs the live transcript** — the lessons extraction then happens later, in the conversation half of the repo's scheduled `growth-extract` task (MCP-native, with a rethink window), so there is nothing to schedule and no in-session lessons pass ([the pack README](../../../../packs/grow_with_claudinite/README.md) owns the standard). A later merge in the same session just runs capture again — it captures the delta. In the rare repo that removed the `grow_with_claudinite` pack from `.claudinite-checks.json`, skip this step.

## Don't

- **Don't** re-read the issue to confirm it closed — `Closes #<issue>` does that on merge; trust it.
